summary.headline: Aster DM Quality Care Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR 2,829 crore, with operating EBITDA up 25% to INR 678 crore at a 24% margin (combined basis).
summary.overview: First full quarter after the Aster DM Healthcare and Quality Care merger, reported on a combined pro forma basis. Revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 2,829 crore, operating EBITDA 25% to INR 678 crore, and normalised PAT (after NCI) 34% to INR 281 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose 20% to INR 5,429 crore and operating EBITDA 27% to INR 1,255 crore. Synergies of INR 16.6 crore were realised in the quarter, a run-rate of about INR 65 crore against a stated potential of about INR 200 crore. Management said reported numbers are not comparable YoY because prior periods were not restated, and it declined to split Aster and Quality Care figures.

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,719 crore; net debt/EBITDA 0.87x excl. leases, 1.72x incl. leases (TTM)
over INR 400 crore, mostly ongoing projects plus medical equipment

segments.name: Mature hospitals (>3 years old, EBITDA margin 25%+)
segments.commentary: 64% of operational beds, 73% of hospital revenue and 83% of operating EBITDA; revenue +18% on 11% patient volume growth. Management cited a 30.2% operating EBITDA margin for this segment on an H1 basis.

segments.name: Focus hospitals
segments.commentary: 15% of operational beds and 15% of revenue; patient volume +7%, revenue +13%. Margins are below 25% but improving for five to six quarters.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (new launches)
segments.commentary: 10% of operational beds and 6% of revenue; patient volume +53%, revenue +62%, led by Kasaragod and Nagercoil.

segments.name: Underperforming hospitals
segments.commentary: 11% of beds and about 5% of revenue; revenue +24%, operating EBITDA more than doubled (over 700 bps margin gain in H1).

guidance_outlook: Synergies: management expects the INR 200 crore full potential to be reached on a run-rate basis by about the fourth quarter, and full realisation by the sixth or seventh quarter. Synergies are expected to be front-loaded.

Margin: 24%-25% full-year operating EBITDA margin targeted two to three years post-merger, including synergies, greenfield turnarounds and about 1,800-2,000+ brownfield beds. Management said Q3 and Q4 are festive quarters with seasonally lower margins.
Capacity: bed base to rise from 10,840 to over 15,000 beds; pipeline of 4,230 beds, about 47% brownfield and 53% greenfield. Aster Trivandrum (454 beds) is on schedule for FY27.
Greenfield losses expected to be negligible: Whitefield broke even in 3 months, Nagercoil in 4 months and Kasaragod in 9 months.
Management said it may pursue acquisitions, citing a good war chest.
capex_capacity: Operational beds up 4% YoY, mainly from Kasaragod and Whitefield Block D; occupancy up 335 bps to 68% as occupied beds grew 8%. Roughly 10,600 operational beds, of which about 80-81% are census and about 20% non-census.
Over INR 1,200 crore invested in project, growth and refresh capex over the last 18 months; over INR 600 crore in medical technology over the same period.
Q2 FY27 medical tech additions: one LINAC, one digital PET-CT, three robots, two cath labs and one MRI.
New Centres of Excellence this quarter: ARISE Robotic Spine Institute (Aster CMI), CARE Cancer Institute (Raipur), Foetal Medicine Centre (Aster Medcity).
Around 2,000 beds to be added to the mature segment via brownfield expansion; management said these beds would be productive from day zero.
demand_pricing: Patients served 2.2 million in Q2 FY27, up 12% YoY, with more complex care mix.
Complex care growth: robotic surgeries +39%, kidney transplants +31%, joint replacements +29%.
CONGO revenue grew more than 16% and non-CONGO more than 19% in the quarter; dengue-related medical cases were cited as a boost in some geographies.
Management stated that the oncology drug price cap affects only specific drugs and has no current impact, and that nearly 75% of operations are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

Management said the sector needs about 1.5 million beds over 10 years, implying about $130 billion of investment; it stated it would engage constructively with Kerala on proposed comprehensive hospital price controls.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR 200 crore synergy be spread evenly over three years, and is it front-loaded?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna said the synergies will be skewed to the front, with the run-rate fully reflected over the next three to four quarters. The INR 65 crore run-rate was reached in the first quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the incremental procurement savings from centralised consumables buying, and what is the gross margin benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number. It said synergies come from a 10-point wheel (clinical, material cost, talent sharing, indirect costs, IT, F&B insourcing, renewable energy and others). It said 30% of articles were previously bought cheaper by one entity, and rates were moved to the lowest common price.

qa_highlights.question: Will the synergies be fully realised within the next three to four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kumar M R said the run-rate reaches INR 65 crore already, the full run-rate is expected by the fourth quarter, and the full amount by the sixth or seventh quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue, EBITDA and margin be split for Aster and Quality Care separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined. It said all numbers are combined, the books and monthly MIS are not split by brand, and the group reviews all 38 hospitals together.

qa_highlights.question: Will greenfield losses offset synergies, creating a J-curve in 2029?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kumar M R said greenfield losses are negligible, as Whitefield broke even in three months, Nagercoil in four months and Kasaragod in nine months, and that synergies act as a backup.

qa_highlights.question: How should the mature segment margin of 30.2% and its incremental flow-through be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna cited efficiency gains as larger hospitals scale, brownfield additions of about 2,000 beds, robotics, quaternary care and ALOS, and said capacity bottlenecks will be addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook from the 24% Q2 base, and does the Q2 base hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil said H1 is 23.1%, Q3 and Q4 are seasonally weaker, and the guidance is 24%-25% full-year in two to three years. The company is not treating one quarter as the base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of possible Kerala-wide price control on hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna said the outcome is hard to predict and that the company will engage constructively with the government. He argued private care provides 65% of India's care and that the sector needs economic returns to attract investment.

risks_watch: Possible state-level price control on hospitals in Kerala, following an assembly committee recommendation that management did not rule out; the oncology drug price cap is said to have no current impact.
Synergy delivery: only INR 16.6 crore booked in Q2, with the full INR 200 crore dependent on execution over six to seven quarters.
Reporting: prior periods are not restated and Aster and Quality Care are not reported separately, which limits like-for-like tracking.
Execution of 4,230 beds (about 1,800-2,000 brownfield) and greenfield ramp-up; margin target depends on them.
Seasonality: Q3 and Q4 are expected to show lower margins than Q2.
Acquisitions are possible, which could add funding or integration risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating and financial delivery, with the company citing record revenue, EBITDA and margin. Guidance is framed cautiously (24%-25% margin in two to three years, and seasonal Q3/Q4 softness). Management was evasive on the separate Aster and Quality Care figures and on the Kerala price-control question, answering at a macro level.
